# origin network commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py from `origin --help` of the release scripts/origin-cli.version pins (v1.14.0).
     Do not edit by hand: fix the help text in origincloudhq/cli, or scripts/cli_reference_overrides.yml, and rerun. -->

This page lists every `origin network` command. Regional resources take `--region`, zonal ones `--zone`; for how both default, see [Use the CLI](../../platform/access/cli.md#set-a-default-project-zone-and-region).

## origin network

Network service: VPCs, subnets, route tables, ACLs, security groups, gateways, floating IPs, network interfaces and DNS policies. Resource names are given as their parts (`--project`, `--region` or `--zone`, `--vpc`), or the resource's flag takes a whole name. VPCs, route tables, ACLs, security groups, internet gateways and DNS policies are regional (`--region`); subnets, network interfaces, floating IPs and NAT gateways are zonal (`--zone`). `--project`, `--zone` and `--region` default to `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` and `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else to the profile's `default-project`, `default-zone` and `region`; `--region`, else to the region of the default zone.

Every `origin network` command also accepts:

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--endpoint <URL>` | Base URL to send the calls to, such as a test server's, instead of the service's own host: `https://network.origincloudapis.eu`, or `https://network.{region}.origincloudapis.eu` when the profile names a `region`. It must be `https://`, or `http://` to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). A list without `--zone` looks up the zones at the location service, not here; `ORIGINCLOUD_LOCATION_ENDPOINT` sends that lookup elsewhere. Environment variable: `ORIGINCLOUD_NETWORK_ENDPOINT`. |

### get-acl

Returns an ACL.

```sh
origin network get-acl [OPTIONS] --acl <ACL>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--acl <ACL>` | yes | The ACL to return. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/acls/{acl}`. |

### list-acls

Lists the ACLs in a region, oldest first.

```sh
origin network list-acls [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most ACLs to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--vpc <VPC>` | no | Only the ACLs of this VPC, when set. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/vpcs/{vpc}`. |

### create-acl

Creates an ACL in a VPC, with no rules: it drops everything until rules are added. The operation is done once the ACL is recorded.

```sh
origin network create-acl [OPTIONS] --vpc <VPC>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--vpc <VPC>` | yes | The VPC the ACL belongs to, in the same project and region. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/vpcs/{vpc}`. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of creating a second ACL. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### update-acl

Changes an ACL's tags. The operation is done once the change is recorded.

```sh
origin network update-acl [OPTIONS] --acl <ACL> <--tag <KEY=VALUE>|--no-tags>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--acl <ACL>` | yes | The acl to change. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/acls/{acl}`. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | one of `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-tags` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-tags` | one of `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Remove all of its tags. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of changing the ACL again. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### delete-acl

Deletes an ACL with its rules. Refused for an ACL the platform created with its VPC, which goes with the VPC, and while an ACL association names it. The operation is done once the change is recorded; the network applies it within seconds.

```sh
origin network delete-acl [OPTIONS] --acl <ACL>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--acl <ACL>` | yes | The ACL to delete. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/acls/{acl}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### create-acl-rule

Adds a rule to an ACL. Refused with `FAILED_PRECONDITION` when a rule of the same direction has the same `--priority`. An ACL holds at most 40 rules by default, both directions together, as the quota sets. The operation is done once the change is recorded; the network applies it within seconds.

```sh
origin network create-acl-rule [OPTIONS] --acl <ACL> --direction <DIRECTION> --priority <PRIORITY> --protocol <PROTOCOL> --cidr-block <CIDR_BLOCK> --action <ACTION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--acl <ACL>` | yes | The `{acl}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--direction <DIRECTION>` | yes | Which traffic the rule applies to. Possible values: `INGRESS`, `EGRESS`. |
| `--priority <PRIORITY>` | yes | The rule's place in its direction, from 1; lower comes first. No two rules of a direction share one. |
| `--protocol <PROTOCOL>` | yes | The traffic the rule matches. Possible values: `ALL`, `TCP`, `UDP`, `ICMP`. |
| `--first-port <FIRST_PORT>` | no | The first port the rule matches, for `TCP` and `UDP`. Each set of ports has one spelling, and the rule reads back in it: `--first-port` 0 and `--last-port` 0 match every port, a `--last-port` of 0 the single port `--first-port`, and a `--first-port` below `--last-port` the range between them. Any other spelling of a set is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the one to use: `--first-port` 22 and `--last-port` 22 is `--first-port` 22 and `--last-port` 0, and 0 or 1 to 65535 is 0 and 0. |
| `--last-port <LAST_PORT>` | no | The last port the rule matches, above `--first-port`; 0 for the single port `--first-port`, or with `--first-port` 0 for every port. |
| `--cidr-block <CIDR_BLOCK>` | yes | The far side's range: where entering traffic comes from, or where leaving traffic goes to. |
| `--action <ACTION>` | yes | What the rule does with the traffic it matches. Possible values: `ACCEPT`, `DROP`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of adding the rule again. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### create-dns-policy

Creates a DNS policy. It isn't the default: associate it with a VPC, or make it the default with `SetDefaultDnsPolicy`. The operation is done once the DNS policy is recorded.

```sh
origin network create-dns-policy [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--relay-enabled <true|false>` | no | Whether the resolver relays names it can't answer itself to `--upstream-server`. Off, it answers only the platform's own names. Possible values: `true`, `false`. |
| `--upstream-server <UPSTREAM_SERVER>` | no | The resolvers to relay to, at most 5 IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, tried in order. At least one while `--relay-enabled` is on. Repeat for more. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of creating a second DNS policy. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### update-dns-policy

Changes a DNS policy's relay settings or tags. The operation is done once the change is recorded; the resolvers of every VPC relaying through the policy apply it within seconds.

```sh
origin network update-dns-policy [OPTIONS] --dns-policy <DNS_POLICY> <--relay-enabled <true|false>|--upstream-server <UPSTREAM_SERVER>|--no-upstream-servers|--tag <KEY=VALUE>|--no-tags>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--dns-policy <DNS_POLICY>` | yes | The dns policy to change. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/dnsPolicies/{dns_policy}`. |
| `--relay-enabled <true|false>` | one of `--relay-enabled`, `--upstream-server`, `--no-upstream-servers`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Whether the resolver relays names it can't answer itself to `--upstream-server`. Off, it answers only the platform's own names. Left as it is when not given. Possible values: `true`, `false`. |
| `--upstream-server <UPSTREAM_SERVER>` | one of `--relay-enabled`, `--upstream-server`, `--no-upstream-servers`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | The resolvers to relay to, at most 5 IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, tried in order. At least one while `--relay-enabled` is on. Repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-upstream-servers` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-upstream-servers` | one of `--relay-enabled`, `--upstream-server`, `--no-upstream-servers`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Remove all of its upstream servers. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | one of `--relay-enabled`, `--upstream-server`, `--no-upstream-servers`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-tags` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-tags` | one of `--relay-enabled`, `--upstream-server`, `--no-upstream-servers`, `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Remove all of its tags. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of changing the DNS policy again. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### set-default-dns-policy

Makes a DNS policy the project's default in its region, in place of the one before. Every VPC of the region without a DNS policy association relays through it from then on. Making the default the default changes nothing. The operation is done once the change is recorded; the resolvers apply it within seconds.

```sh
origin network set-default-dns-policy [OPTIONS] --dns-policy <DNS_POLICY>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--dns-policy <DNS_POLICY>` | yes | The DNS policy to make the default. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/dnsPolicies/{dns_policy}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

| `--vpc <VPC>` | no | The `{vpc}` part of the resource names the command builds. Needed unless `--dns-policy-association` is given a whole name, which has it. |
| `--dns-policy-association <DNS_POLICY_ASSOCIATION>` | yes | The association to return. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region` and `--vpc`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/vpcs/{vpc}/dnsPolicyAssociations/{dns_policy_association}`. |

### create-floating-ip

Allocates a floating IP from the zone's public addresses, associated with nothing. The operation is done once the address is recorded as yours.


| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |

| Option | Required | Description |

| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### create-security-group-rule

Adds a rule to a security group. A rule identical to one the group has in every field, `--description` included, is refused with `FAILED_PRECONDITION`. A group holds at most 120 rules by default, both directions together, as the quota sets. The operation is done once the change is recorded; the network applies it within seconds.

```sh
origin network create-security-group-rule [OPTIONS] --security-group <SECURITY_GROUP> --direction <DIRECTION> --protocol <PROTOCOL>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--security-group <SECURITY_GROUP>` | yes | The `{security_group}` part of the resource names the command builds. |
| `--direction <DIRECTION>` | yes | Which traffic the rule applies to. Possible values: `INGRESS`, `EGRESS`. |
| `--protocol <PROTOCOL>` | yes | The traffic the rule allows. Possible values: `ALL`, `TCP`, `UDP`, `ICMP`. |
| `--first-port <FIRST_PORT>` | no | The first port the rule matches, for `TCP` and `UDP`. Each set of ports has one spelling, and the rule reads back in it: `--first-port` 0 and `--last-port` 0 match every port, a `--last-port` of 0 the single port `--first-port`, and a `--first-port` below `--last-port` the range between them. Any other spelling of a set is refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT` naming the one to use: `--first-port` 22 and `--last-port` 22 is `--first-port` 22 and `--last-port` 0, and 0 or 1 to 65535 is 0 and 0. |
| `--last-port <LAST_PORT>` | no | The last port the rule matches, above `--first-port`; 0 for the single port `--first-port`, or with `--first-port` 0 for every port. |
| `--cidr-block <CIDR_BLOCK>` | no | The peer as an address range: where admitted traffic comes from, or where sent traffic goes to. |
| `--peer-security-group <SECURITY_GROUP>` | no | The peer as another security group of the same VPC: its members' addresses. The rule's own group is refused here with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`: it is `--same-group`. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/securityGroups/{security_group}`. |
| `--same-group <true|false>` | no | The peer as the rule's own group's members. Possible values: `true`, `false`. |
| `--description <DESCRIPTION>` | no | What the rule is for. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of adding the rule again. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-vpc

Returns a VPC.

```sh
origin network get-vpc [OPTIONS] --vpc <VPC>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--vpc <VPC>` | yes | The VPC to return. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/vpcs/{vpc}`. |

### list-vpcs

Lists the VPCs in a region, oldest first.

```sh
origin network list-vpcs [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--page-size <PAGE_SIZE>` | no | The most VPCs to return; the server clamps it, and 0 means its default. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |
| `--page-token <PAGE_TOKEN>` | no | A previous response's `nextPageToken`, for the page after it. Without `--page-size` or `--page-token`, every page is listed. |

### create-vpc

Creates an empty VPC: no subnets, security groups, ACLs, route tables or internet gateway. It relays DNS through the project's default DNS policy in its region until a DNS policy association names another. The operation is done once the VPC is recorded.

```sh
origin network create-vpc [OPTIONS]
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--ipv4-cidr-block <IPV4_CIDR_BLOCK>` | no | The private IPv4 range (RFC 1918), from `/16` to `/28`. A free `/16` of the `172.16` private block when left empty. Subnets are carved from it in equal sizes. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | no | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of creating a second VPC. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### update-vpc

Changes a VPC's tags. The operation is done once the change is recorded.

```sh
origin network update-vpc [OPTIONS] --vpc <VPC> <--tag <KEY=VALUE>|--no-tags>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--vpc <VPC>` | yes | The vpc to change. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/vpcs/{vpc}`. |
| `--tag <KEY=VALUE>` | one of `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Labels of your own, at most 50. The `origin:name` tag is the name the console shows. As KEY=VALUE; repeat for more. Replaces all of them, so give every one to keep; `--no-tags` removes them all. Left as they are when neither is given. |
| `--no-tags` | one of `--tag`, `--no-tags` | Remove all of its tags. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation instead of changing the VPC again. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |

### delete-vpc

Deletes a VPC with its DNS policy association. Refused with `FAILED_PRECONDITION` while the VPC has subnets, security groups, ACLs, route tables or an internet gateway, except those the platform created with it, which are deleted with it. The operation is done once the change is recorded; the network applies it within seconds.

```sh
origin network delete-vpc [OPTIONS] --vpc <VPC>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--region <REGION>` | no | The region, such as `eu-central1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_REGION`, else the profile's `region`, else the region of the default zone (`ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE` or `default-zone`), when not given. |
| `--vpc <VPC>` | yes | The VPC to delete. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--region`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/regions/{region}/vpcs/{vpc}`. |
| `--request-id <REQUEST_ID>` | no | A UUID; a repeat with the same id returns the first request's operation. One is generated when not given. |
| `--no-wait` | no | Print the operation as soon as the API accepts it, instead of waiting until it is done. |
| `--yes` | no | Confirm an irreversible operation: a delete, or a change the help says can't be undone. Without it the command refuses, and says what it would have done, before sending anything. |

### get-operation

Returns an operation as it is now. The operation is one an `origin network` command answered with, such as the one `--no-wait` prints.

```sh
origin network get-operation [OPTIONS] --operation <OPERATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--operation <OPERATION>` | yes | The operation. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/operations/{operation}`. |

### wait-operation

Waits until an operation is done or `--timeout` has passed, whichever comes first, and returns it as it is then. It only reads, so a client may repeat it after a transport error. The operation is one an `origin network` command answered with, such as the one `--no-wait` prints. Without `--timeout`, the command waits until the operation is done; Ctrl-C stops the waiting, not the operation. It prints the operation, and exits with status 1 when the operation failed, or isn't done when `--timeout` passes.

```sh
origin network wait-operation [OPTIONS] --operation <OPERATION>
```

| Option | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--project <PROJECT>` | no | The project, such as `my-project-123`. `ORIGINCLOUD_PROJECT`, else the profile's `default-project`, when not given. |
| `--zone <ZONE>` | no | The zone, such as `eu-central1-az1`. `ORIGINCLOUD_ZONE`, else the profile's `default-zone`, when not given. |
| `--operation <OPERATION>` | yes | The operation. Its id, completed with `--project` and `--zone`, or its whole name, `projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/operations/{operation}`. |
| `--timeout <DURATION>` | no | How long to wait for the operation, such as `30s` or `5m`. Without it, the command waits as long as the operation takes. When it passes first, the command prints the operation as it is and exits with status 1. |
